## Context / Problem

RP-04 S1 advisory review finding (change 1841 PS3). The AC1 cross-surface equivalence contract
in `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_operation_snapshot_surfaces.py` claims that CLI, public
Python, MCP, and the direct reconciler entry point all compose the same `OperationSnapshot`.
Its "MCP surface" and "reconciler surface" blocks do not drive those surfaces at all: each
re-calls `compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=..., cli_overrides=...)` with arguments
identical to the Python block, then asserts the three results are equal. That is trivially
true, so the block stays green even if the MCP tools or the reconciler entry point stopped
routing through the shared composer — which is precisely the parity bug the contract exists to
catch.

## Approach

Drive the real entry points and assert on what they actually composed.

- MCP: build a real server with `rebar.mcp_server.build_server()` and drive a real tool call
  via `asyncio.run(server.call_tool(...))` — the pattern already used by `_call_read_tool` in
  `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_mcp_survives_non_repo_root_176d.py:26`. Use
  `explain_criterion` (`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:245`), a pure registry read with no store,
  LLM, or network dependency, whose first action is `_shadow("mcp.read.explain_criterion")`
  at `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:253`.
- Reconciler: call `rebar_reconciler.__main__.main()` with argv. `main` composes its snapshot
  at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:570` (`_emit_operation_shadow`)
  immediately after request normalization, and `--dry-run-enumerate`
  (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/request.py:75`) returns at `__main__.py:573`, before
  any advisory lock, pass, or network effect.
- Capture: both surfaces reach the composer through
  `rebar._operation_config.emit_shadow_snapshot`, which calls the module global
  `compose_operation_snapshot` at `src/rebar/_operation_config.py:251` — a name resolved from
  module globals at CALL time, so rebinding that module attribute genuinely reaches code
  entered through the real surfaces rather than only the test module's import-time binding. A
  recorder wraps it for the duration of each surface call and returns the real composer's
  result unchanged, so the driven surface behaves exactly as in production.

Asserting instead on the surface's emitted DEBUG diagnostic was rejected: that line carries
only a 12-hex truncated fingerprint (`src/rebar/_operation_config.py` `emit_shadow_snapshot`),
which can only ever be compared against another composition, reintroducing the same vacuity.

Two properties make the contract discriminate, and both are required:

1. The recorder must have fired. An empty capture list fails with an explicit message, so a
   surface that stops routing through the composer goes RED instead of looping over nothing —
   the failure mode where a spy that never fires is indistinguishable from a passing assertion.
2. Each surface's own snapshot is anchored to ABSOLUTE expected content (repo root, envelope
   version, and two config keys with distinct provenance) in addition to being compared to the
   Python reference. Cross-surface comparison alone is vacuous: perturb the composer and every
   surface moves together, so "equal to each other" stays true while all of them are wrong.

The shared input moves off `cli_overrides` onto a project layer (`sync.push`) plus an env layer
(`REBAR_VERIFY_MAX_TICKET_DESCRIPTION_CHARS`), because MCP's `_shadow` and the reconciler's
`_emit_operation_shadow` pass no `cli_overrides`. A cli-layer-only anchor can only be asserted
on the surfaces that accept one, which is how the block ended up re-composing instead of
driving. The existing CLI block keeps its own cli-layer provenance assertion.

## Scope

`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_operation_snapshot_surfaces.py` only. No production code
changes; nothing outside this file is edited.

## Testing

The change IS the test, so its discrimination is established by mutation rather than by adding
further tests:

- Perturb `compose_operation_snapshot` to collapse `env` provenance into `project`. The MCP and
  reconciler surface assertions must go RED, and the pre-change version of the file must stay
  GREEN under the same perturbation.
- Neutralize the MCP `_shadow` body and the reconciler `_emit_operation_shadow` body,
  independently. Each surface's "composed no operation snapshot" assertion must go RED naming
  that surface.
- Revert every perturbation; the file must be GREEN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The MCP block invokes the real MCP entry point (`build_server()` + `call_tool`) instead
      of calling the composer again. Checked by reading the file: no `compose_operation_snapshot(`
      call remains in the MCP or reconciler block.
- [ ] The reconciler block invokes the real `rebar_reconciler.__main__.main()` argv entry point
      and asserts its return code is 0. Checked by reading the file and by the test passing.
- [ ] Each surface block fails when its surface composes no snapshot. Checked by neutralizing
      `_shadow` and `_emit_operation_shadow` one at a time and observing a RED assertion that
      names that surface.
- [ ] Perturbing the composer makes the surface assertions RED. Checked by applying the
      env-to-project provenance perturbation and observing the MCP/reconciler assertions fail,
      then reverting and observing GREEN; the pre-change file stays GREEN under the same
      perturbation.
- [ ] Gates pass on the whole tree: `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reporting `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`,
      and `pytest tests --ignore=tests/external`.
